subcriteria.name: Relevance to Emergent Phenomena
subcriteria.question: Does the research explicitly address emergent phenomena at the mesoscale in molecular/cellular biosciences?

levels.label: Not relevant; does not address emergent phenomena
Minimally relevant; tangential connection to emergent phenomena
Moderately relevant; addresses emergent phenomena but not as central focus
Highly relevant; emergent phenomena is a key focus
Exceptionally relevant; directly and explicitly addresses mesoscale emergent phenomena

subcriteria.name: Novelty & Significance
subcriteria.question: Are the questions and approaches innovative? Do they have potential to advance knowledge?

levels.label: Not novel; incremental work with limited significance
Somewhat novel; modest advancement expected
Novel; clear advancement in the field
Highly novel; significant potential to advance knowledge
Groundbreaking; transformative potential for the field

subcriteria.name: Rigor of Approach
subcriteria.question: Is the proposed methodology clear, logical, and grounded in established or emerging research practices?

levels.label: Poor; unclear or illogical methodology
Fair; methodology has significant gaps or concerns
Good; solid methodology with minor concerns
Very good; clear, logical, and well-grounded methodology
Excellent; exceptionally rigorous and well-justified approach

subcriteria.name: Scope & Timeline
subcriteria.question: Are the goals and milestones realistic for the proposed time frame and planned approach?

levels.label: Unrealistic; goals are unattainable within proposed timeline
Questionable; significant concerns about feasibility
Reasonable; achievable with noted challenges
Realistic; well-planned scope and timeline
Highly feasible; excellent planning with contingencies

subcriteria.name: Synthesis Focus
subcriteria.question: Does the proposal clearly demonstrate a synthesis project?

levels.label: No synthesis; appears to be primarily generating new data
Minimal synthesis; mostly new data generation with some integration
Moderate synthesis; balanced between existing and new data
Strong synthesis; primarily uses existing data with clear integration plan
Exemplary synthesis; exclusively uses existing data with comprehensive integration

subcriteria.name: Data Identification
subcriteria.question: Are the data sources explicitly identified, and are limitations appropriately acknowledged?

levels.label: Poor; data sources vague and limitations not addressed
Fair; some data sources identified but incomplete or limitations ignored
Good; data sources identified and basic limitations acknowledged
Very good; clear data sources with thoughtful discussion of limitations
Excellent; comprehensive data source specification with thorough limitation analysis

subcriteria.name: Open Science Commitment
subcriteria.question: Does the proposal demonstrate a commitment to open, team, and reproducible science principles?

levels.label: No commitment; does not address open science
Minimal commitment; vague statements without concrete plans
Moderate commitment; some open science practices mentioned
Strong commitment; clear plans for open and reproducible science
Exemplary commitment; comprehensive open science framework with detailed implementation
